papers.title: Unveiling digital narratives of transnational migration to China: foreign wanghong on Douyin and Xiaohongshu
papers.authors: Xintian Li, Yihui Zheng, and Guodong Du
papers.category: 甲亢哥访华 · adjacent foreign-influencer mechanism
papers.evidence: Publisher or authoritative scholarly-index record verified
papers.takeaway: This mixed-methods study combines critical discourse analysis and framing theory to examine how Chinese users perceive foreign wanghong active on Douyin and Xiaohongshu. It analyzes 1,074 Douyin comments and 1,493 Xiaohongshu comments and identifies frames of nationalist backlash and othering, language and cultural humor, exoticism and admiration, integration and assimilation, and national pride and normalization. The article is adjacent rather than direct evidence for the IShowSpeed idea because it studies Chinese audiences’ responses to foreign creators, not foreign followers’ attitudes toward China after observing an influencer visit.

papers.title: The Impact of Artificial Intelligence Usage on Affective Work Well-Being: A Self-Determination Theory Perspective
papers.authors: Chi Zhang, Shuping Chen, Dianru Zhang, and Qichao Zhang
papers.category: Workplace AI and well-being · direct evidence
papers.evidence: Publisher or authoritative scholarly-index record verified
papers.takeaway: A three-wave time-lagged survey of 360 employees tests how workplace AI use relates to affective work well-being. AI use positively predicts affective well-being through two parallel mediators, work meaningfulness and work engagement, and higher-quality human–AI collaboration strengthens both indirect paths. The temporal separation improves measurement ordering, but the self-report observational design does not establish that AI use causes the reported gains.

papers.title: Generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) use, work outcomes, and the moderating role of GenAI literacy in early organizational adoption
papers.venue: Computers in Human Behavior: Artificial Humans, 6, 100380
papers.category: Workplace AI and well-being · direct engagement and meaningful-work evidence
papers.evidence: Publisher or authoritative scholarly-index record verified
papers.takeaway: A cross-sectional online survey of 1,001 administrative employees at a global industrial company was conducted shortly before an organization-wide GenAI rollout in early 2025. Structural equation models show small positive associations between GenAI-use frequency and work engagement and quantitative job performance. GenAI literacy moderates associations with qualitative performance, quantitative performance, and meaningfulness of work, indicating that access alone is not uniformly beneficial. The design captures an important pre-transformation stage but remains correlational and does not measure broad life satisfaction.

papers.title: How Does AI Exacerbate Job Burnout Among Media Professionals? A Multi-Logic Analysis Integrating JD-R and COR
papers.category: Preprint · workplace AI and well-being · not peer reviewed
papers.evidence: Publisher or authoritative scholarly-index record verified
papers.takeaway: This working paper examines how AI-related work conditions contribute to burnout among media professionals by integrating the Job Demands–Resources model with Conservation of Resources theory. It models AI as a source of changing demands and resource pressures rather than assuming a uniformly positive productivity effect, and it focuses directly on occupational burnout in an AI-intensive profession. The repository record was first posted on 4 September 2026. The paper has not completed journal peer review, so its findings should be treated as provisional.

toc.title: At what cost? Unintended lateral effects of persuasive messages linking liked and disliked concepts
toc.abstractEn: An experiment with 1,002 participants tests persuasive messages that connect negatively evaluated flies with positively evaluated pollinators and butterflies. The linkage improves the targeted attitude toward flies but produces negative lateral change in attitudes toward the liked concepts. The authors interpret the pattern as a possible consequence of resolving cognitive inconsistency and argue that campaign design should evaluate effects beyond the focal attitude.

toc.title: Narrative character networks are associated with storytelling success
toc.abstractEn: A computational analysis of more than 10,000 novels and 1,000 film screenplays represents stories as networks of characters and interactions. Lower clustering is associated with novel popularity and film ratings, while modularity predicts novel popularity and shorter paths predict film ratings. The study provides a scalable way to connect narrative structure with storytelling success.

toc.title: Technology-mediated communication among migrant families separated by borders: understanding the tensions of relational maintenance
toc.abstractEn: Interviews with 27 Latina/o/x/e family triads examine technology-mediated relationship maintenance during migration-based separation. Routine contact, real-time interaction, and selective disclosure repeatedly create tensions, while structural barriers and cultural norms distribute relational costs unevenly across family members.

toc.title: The invisible labor of assimilation by individuals with stigmatized identities: a qualitative study of autistic workers’ organizational socialization
toc.abstractEn: Interviews with 31 autistic workers develop the concept of assimilation labor: deliberate, sustained, and often invisible work required to adapt to neuronormative organizational expectations. The study identifies structural conditions and individual practices that generate disproportionate socialization burdens.

toc.title: Relationship uncertainty and person-specific dynamics of partner rumination and relational turbulence in day-to-day life
toc.abstractEn: Intensive day-to-day data are used to examine within-person links among relationship uncertainty, partner-focused rumination, and relational turbulence. The study emphasizes person-specific dynamics rather than assuming a single average process across couples and clarifies how uncertainty and rumination vary together over time.

papers.title: Western Audience Reception of Chinese Cultural IP in Ne Zha 2: An LDA and Critical Metaphor Analysis of Film Reviews
papers.evidence: Publisher or authoritative scholarly-index record verified
papers.takeaway: The study analyzes 658 English-language reviews of Ne Zha 2 from IMDb and Rotten Tomatoes using latent Dirichlet allocation and critical metaphor analysis. It identifies recurring themes in Western viewers’ evaluations and shows that reviews often translate the film’s culturally embedded conflicts into familiar individual-rebellion frames while assessing visual and narrative qualities through established Western cinematic benchmarks. The article provides unusually direct evidence about foreign reception of a Chinese mythological character, but platform reviewers are self-selected and the observational text analysis cannot separate comprehension, liking, character identification, and sharing intention as distinct outcomes.

papers.title: Narrative Strategies and Audience Reception in the Reimagining of Chinese Mythology
papers.authors: Xing Enhe and Myung Jin Park
papers.venue: Journal of Chinese Language and Literature, 102, 241–270
papers.evidence: Publisher or authoritative scholarly-index record verified
papers.takeaway: This comparative study examines Creation of the Gods II and Ne Zha II through narrative structure, visual signs, and audience responses. It finds that Creation of the Gods II uses a multi-linear epic structure centered on collective heroes, political order, historical legitimacy, and cultural continuity, whereas Ne Zha II builds a single-line growth narrative around personal experience, self-redemption, resistance to fate, and modern subjectivity. The reception component helps connect formal narrative choices with audience evaluation, but the study does not isolate foreign audiences or experimentally distinguish value congruence, moral evaluation, cultural proximity, identification, and transmission intention.
